chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-'Ubaydi, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far, who said:
The Faqih, peace be upon him, said: "The end of the time of the 'asr prayer is six and a half feet."

As for what has been narrated in the reports that we presented earlier, that the time extends until sunset, it is to be understood as referring to one who has excuses and one who has a necessity that prevents him from the salat (prayer), as we have explained. And similarly is to be understood what he narrated:

key_terms.آخِرُ وَقْتِ الْعَصْرِ: the ending point of the prescribed time for the 'asr prayer
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: narrations or reports transmitted on the issue
key_terms.سِتَّةُ أَقْدَامٍ وَنِصْفٌ: a measured limit used here to define the end of the normal prayer time
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الْأَعْذَارِ: a person possessing legally recognized excuses

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith explain the end time of the 'asr prayer and the reports extending it until sunset?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal timing of the 'asr prayer and distinguishes between the standard end time and an extended time granted to those with valid excuses or necessity. It reflects a juristic reconciliation between narrations by interpreting the extension until sunset as applying specifically to people under constraint.
